paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

extraction.paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Section V experimental setup and Fig. 5 / Fig. 6 (MTTF results)
scenario.description: Simulated 8x8 NoC-based many-core system (16nm, 109 mm^2 squared floorplan, TDP 90 W) running 25 randomly selected multi-threaded PARSEC applications under the proposed thermal-cycling-aware resource manager (mapping, scheduling, DPM) compared with a nominal baseline, MOC, and reliability-aware mapping. The reported observable is per-core thermal-cycling MTTF (years), summarized as MIN, STD and AVG. Only total chip area and TDP are published; no per-block coordinates, dimensions or per-block power values are given.
scenario.architecture: 8x8 homogeneous mesh NoC many-core, Niagara2-like SPARC cores, private L1 and distributed shared L2, four memory controllers, per-core DVFS and PCPG, per-core temperature sensors
scenario.workload: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmarks, 25 randomly selected application executions issued at runtime
scenario.operating_point: TDP 90 W, 16nm, chip area 109 mm^2; thermal cycling model EaTC=0.42 eV, b=2.35, Tth=1 C, A_TC fitted for MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C, 1 hour, m=10; temperature sampling about 1 s

original_setup.solver: Noculator (shared-memory NoC-based many-core simulator built on Intel PIN) with McPAT/Lumos power and scaling parameters, and HotSpot steady-state thermal model integrated; thermal-cycling reliability computed via rainflow counting, Miner's rule and Coffin-Manson (Eqs. 1-3) (PDF p.2, p.5)
original_setup.optimizer: Heuristic reliability-aware runtime resource management: RAF affinity-based mapping extending MapPro (Algorithm 2), temperature-deviation-sorted round-robin thread scheduling (Algorithm 3), and DPM extending MOC with a thermal-cycling metric avgAmplitude x maxT (PDF p.3-5)
original_setup.controller: Global feedback controller with reliability analysis unit (about 1 s sampling, 1-2 h long-term period), reliability-aware mapping, thread scheduling (few ms period), and DPM with PID stage plus multi-objective control of per-core DVFS and PCPG under 90 W TDP (PDF p.3-5)
original_setup.benchmark: 8x8 homogeneous many-core (Niagara2/SPARC cores, 16nm, 109 mm^2, TDP 90 W) running 25 randomly selected multi-threaded PARSEC application executions, compared against nominal baseline, MOC and reliability-aware mapping [2] (PDF p.5)

thermal_observable.location: Per core of the 8x8 many-core; Fig. 5 per-core MTTF snapshot and Fig. 6 summary (MIN, STD, AVG); no numeric values are given in the text, only relative improvements (min MTTF +54%, +51%, +39%; avg +40%, +21%, +20% vs baseline, MOC, RA-mapping)
thermal_observable.aggregation: Per-core MTTF_TC from rainflow cycles and Miner's rule over the run; summarized as minimum, standard deviation and average across cores after 25 application executions

physical_mismatches.reason: The study is a system-level reliability and resource-management evaluation: the observable is thermal-cycling MTTF (years), not a steady-state temperature field, so it cannot be compared directly to a steady 2D thermal solve.

Transient, workload-driven dynamics are essential (temperature traces sampled about 1 s, rainflow cycle extraction, ms-scale scheduling, 1-2 h control epochs, random application arrivals); a single-row steady power trace cannot reproduce the thermal-cycling amplitude and frequency.
The controller (PID plus multi-objective DPM, mapping unit, scheduler, PCPG and DVFS) and the heuristic optimizer are not representable in a static placement or thermal solve.
Original thermal solver is HotSpot steady-state with unspecified package, cooling and material parameters; the cooling and interposer are not described, and no 3D stacking is involved.

No per-core or per-block geometry (x, y, width, height) and no per-block power are published; only total chip area 109 mm^2, an 8x8 squared floorplan and a 90 W TDP, so splitting power would require an unpublished rule.
Reliability results (MTTF fitted so MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C) depend on the Coffin-Manson model parameters, which the Studio does not model.

methods.note: Text on PDF pp.2-5 supports the described methods: Coffin-Manson, Miner's rule, rainflow counting, RAF mapping extending MapPro, temperature-deviation scheduling, and MOC-based DPM with avgAmplitude x maxT. The Noculator + McPAT/Lumos + HotSpot steady-state setup is also supported. This is verified from extracted text only. The paper is a system-level reliability and resource-management study with transient traces and a controller. It is not a 2D steady reproduction.

code.note: No code, repository, availability statement or pinned asset is supplied (assets list is empty). The only URLs are the ITRS site and the source PDF. Noculator, MapPro, MOC and the HotSpot setup are cited but not supplied, so no code claim can be verified.

parameters.note: The published scalars match p.5: EaTC=0.42 eV, b=2.35, Tth=1 C, k=8.62e-5 eV/K, calibration at deltaT=20 C, TMax=70 C, 1 h, m=10 giving 10 years, 109 mm^2, 16 nm, TDP 90 W, 25 applications. The p.3 values (about 1 s sampling, 1-2 h long-term period) also match. The fitted A_TC is unpublished. The percent improvements (54/51/39, 40/21/20, 55/43/38) match p.5 text, but the absolute MTTF values behind them are not available.

assessment.summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed false; input_gate_pass false; scientific_gate_pass false). The scenario is a custom_2d_steady experiment with empty floorplan and power_w, so Studio input validity fails (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). As a custom steady run it would have no transient trace in any case. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace asset exists, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated and there is no source commit or generated-placement assumption to report. The paper (W3036764451) is a system-level reliability and resource-management study of an 8x8 many-core (16nm, 109 mm^2, 90 W TDP, 25 PARSEC applications). Its observable is per-core thermal-cycling MTTF in years, reported only as relative improvements (min MTTF +54%/+51%/+39%, avg +40%/+21%/+20%, std +55%/+43%/+38% versus baseline/MOC/RA-mapping). Because no Studio result exists, comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison is made. No exact replication is claimed. Qualitatively, thermal-cycling MTTF depends on temperature amplitude, peak temperature and cycle count from transient, workload-driven dynamics, and a steady 2D solve could at most show spatial hotspot sensitivity, not MTTF. The verdict is determined by the deterministic gate: not_2d_applicable does not run.
limitations: Gate outcome: not_2d_applicable with simulation skipped; the final verdict is controlled by the gate and comparison_valid is false.
No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison to the paper is possible and no replication is claimed.
Mismatch in observable: the paper reports thermal-cycling MTTF in years, not a steady temperature field.

Mismatch in regime: the paper relies on transient dynamics (about 1 s sampling, rainflow counting, ms-scale scheduling, 1-2 h control epochs, random application arrivals), whereas a custom steady 2D run has no transient trace.
Mismatch in aggregation and location: the paper reports per-core MIN, STD and AVG MTTF across 64 cores after 25 application runs; no comparable location or aggregation exists.

Missing geometry and power: only total area 109 mm^2, an 8x8 squared floorplan and a 90 W TDP are published; there are no per-core coordinates, sizes or powers, and splitting TDP would need an unpublished rule.
Boundary assumptions: HotSpot package, heat spreader, heat sink, convection and ambient parameters are unpublished, so boundary conditions cannot be matched.

The controller and heuristic optimizer (PID, multi-objective DPM, RAF mapping, thread scheduling, DVFS, PCPG) cannot be represented in a static thermal solve, and the Coffin-Manson reliability model (A_TC unpublished) is not modeled by Studio.
Only relative improvement percentages are given in the text; Figs. 5 and 6 are not digitized, so absolute MTTF values are unavailable.
Artifact search found no linked code, data or configuration; no Ascend910/ATPlace pinned asset was supplied, so no source commit or placement assumption applies.
Evidence and review problems: one evidence item lacks a valid page or asset locator, there is no cited thermal observable or regime, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved.
